transcript:
User: Hi, we saw your service. Our intake calls after hours keep going to voicemail.
Agent: Got it, thanks for sharing that — those after-hours intake calls going to voicemail are usually where a lot of lost business hides.  

Mhm, when those calls hit voicemail right now, do people usually leave a message, or do they just hang up and call the next place?
User: Most leave a message, but we estimate around 70% would book if someone answered.
Agent: Makes sense, so you’re feeling like if a real person picked up, most of those callers would turn into booked visits instead of just… maybe calling back later.  

So I’m on the same page, what kind of clinic or business are you running?
User: We are a personal injury law firm called 'Bell & Associates Legal' based in New York, NY.
Agent: Got it, Bell & Associates in New York — that helps a lot, thanks.  

So with those after-hours accident/intake calls hitting voicemail, what do you think actually happens with most of those people after they hang up — do they usually wait for you, or do you suspect many just call the next PI firm that actually picks up?
User: I suspect many call the next PI firm that actually picks up, rather than wait for us.
Agent: Yeah, that’s what I hear from a lot of PI firms — the first one who answers usually wins the case.  

So roughly how many new-intake calls a week would you say are hitting voicemail instead of a live answer, especially evenings and weekends?
User: About 12 missed calls a week go to voicemail during those times.
Agent: That’s a lot of potential cases just sitting in voicemail every week.  

Given that, are you actively looking for a way to turn those after-hours calls into booked consults automatically, or are you more so just exploring what’s out there right now?
User: We are actively looking for a solution to convert those after-hours calls into booked consultations automatically.
Agent: Got it, that’s exactly the problem we help PI firms fix.  

Has anyone ever walked you through what those 12 missed after-hours calls a week are actually costing you in lost cases?
User: No, they haven't. But I can tell you the average intake value is about $1,800.
Agent: Right, so doing the math on what you just gave me, those missed after-hours calls are costing you about sixty-five thousand a month in potential case value — just from voicemail.  

So… since you’re actively looking to fix this, it’s a simple 20‑minute walkthrough where we plug *your* numbers in and show exactly how we turn those after-hours calls into booked consults — is it better for you to do that later today, or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow would work best for me. Can you suggest a time?
Agent: Nice, tomorrow works.  

First thing I’ll do is grab your details so we book this in properly — what’s your first name?
User: My name is Marcus Bell.
Agent: Nice to meet you, Marcus.  

For tomorrow, I can get you in as soon as Wednesday at 1:15 PM Eastern or 2:00 PM Eastern — which works better for you?
User: Wednesday at 2:00 PM Eastern works for me. Please book it.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that on our side.
Agent: Perfect, you’re all set — we’re booked for Wednesday at 2:00 PM Eastern. You’ll get a text in a moment with the confirmation and a link to add it to your calendar or reschedule if you need to.

Is there anything else I can help you with before we wrap up?
